Topic: The Transformational View of Derivatives: From Slopes to Sensitivities

Target audience: University students (Calculus I beginners)

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite: The Concept of Rate of Change

Lecture lines:
Measure change over an interval with secant lines.
Visualize squirrel speed: distance divided by time.
Average rate of change forms the foundational baseline.

Planned animations:
Show a static line with two points, A and B. Color #FFD700.
Draw a secant line connecting points A and B. Color #00FFFF.
Show the gap between points A and B shrinking. Color #FF4500.

Section: section_2 — The Geometric Transition: Zooming In

Lecture lines:
Zoom into curves with a magnifying glass.
Secant lines transform into local tangent slopes.
The roller coaster segment becomes a straight line.

Planned animations:
Display a smooth curve graph on a grid. Color #FFFFFF.
Show a magnifying glass focusing on a curve segment. Color #00FF00.
Display the local linear approximation (tangent). Color #FF00FF.

Section: section_3 — The Functional View: Sensitivity Analysis

Lecture lines:
Derivatives act as a sensitivity analysis machine.
A tiny input nudge changes the output.
Robotic arm control demonstrates positional sensitivity.

Planned animations:
Display a function input 'x' and output 'f(x)'. Color #FFFFFF.
Highlight the change in x as a small vector. Color #FFFF00.
Show the corresponding change in f(x) via projection. Color #00CED1.

Section: section_4 — The Dynamic Operator: Visualizing Change

Lecture lines:
View derivatives as dynamic, transforming operators.
Position functions transform into velocity functions.
Watch the graph morph in real-time.

Planned animations:
Display the derivative operator 'd/dx' as a gear. Color #FFA500.
Show the gear turning to transform a curve. Color #FF4500.
Display the resulting slope output vector. Color #7FFF00.

Section: section_5 — Synthesis and Summary

Lecture lines:
Derivatives transform states into rates of change.
Local linear approximation provides transformational power.
Summarize the path: Function, Derivative, Context.

Planned animations:
Summarize the concept of rate as a path. Color #FFFFFF.
Connect all previously shown visual symbols sequentially. Color #FFD700.
Highlight the final derivative formula with pulse effect. Color #FF0000.

Pedagogical scaffolding for complex topics should follow a clear sequence: (1) Problem Hook, (2) Prerequisites/Baseline, (3) Technical Solution, (4) Conceptual Intuition/Why, and (5) Extensions/Proofs.
Utilize computer science analogies (e.g., two's complement) for abstract number theory to provide familiar mental anchors for learners.
Include at least one animation step that qualitatively visualizes the underlying 'bridge' principle (e.g., circular constraints) when presenting surprising mathematical-physical connections.
To prevent visual obstruction, assign concurrent mobjects to distinct grid cells or non-overlapping areas rather than stacking them on the exact same coordinate, even if they appear sequentially.
